page: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dldsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64 and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes a bundled local storage capacity of 7559 GB and is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance across multiple compute and memory bandwidth tests. The Intel Xeon processor's advanced vector and matrix extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX, contribute to a Passmark CPU extended instructions score of 145,477.27 and a Passmark CPU score of 103,274.51, both placing in the top 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with uncached large-block read speeds reaching 501.02 GB/sec and write speeds at 215.13 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations, which reached 146.84 million operations per second, also rank in the top tier. For LLM inference, the server demonstrates top-tier prompt processing speeds, though text generation for smaller models is relatively weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D128lds_v6 maximizes compute density and local storage capacity at the expense of memory depth. The 2 GB of RAM per vCPU represents a lean memory profile, making it highly cost-effective for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. This hardware configuration is well-suited for high-throughput database operations, multi-threaded data decompression, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning prompt processing.
